condition.label: Osteoporosis
condition.distinctions: Low bone mass/osteopenia in a trial is broader than diagnosed osteoporosis. Vertebral fracture, multiple fragility fractures, fall risk and frailty are attributes requiring separate handling.

scope.population: Adults with osteoporosis; primary lifting trial is selected postmenopausal women over 58 with T-score below −1.0.
scope.stage: Stable low bone mass cohorts; acute vertebral fracture, recent surgery and medically unstable patients are not established by the lifting RCT.
scope.operativeStatus: Primarily nonoperative exercise research; surgical protocols and postoperative clearance not established.
scope.exclusions: LIFTMOR excluded fracture within 12 months, localized back pain, lower limb joint injury/surgery and specified comorbidities/medications. These are study limits, not universal contraindications.
scope.uncertainty: Fracture prevention is not equivalent to BMD improvement; exact safe loads/ranges for an individual are unknown.

sources.design: Evidence review plus expert consensus; boxes distinguish evidence [E] and consensus [C].
sources.population: People with osteoporosis, stratified by vertebral/multiple low-trauma fractures, fall history and frailty.
sources.comparator: Heterogeneous exercise/control studies, not one randomized comparison.
sources.outcomes: Recommends resistance, impact, balance and spinal-extensor approaches. Most spine-sparing and fracture-specific modifications are consensus rather than directly proven risk thresholds.
sources.followUp: Varies by underlying studies; no common follow-up.
sources.uncertainty: Adverse events incompletely reported; theoretical risks must be distinguished from measured harms.
sources.harms: Review notes sparse adverse-event reporting, cases involving spinal flexion and some increased falls/fractures in high-risk walking cohorts; no universal safety established.
sources.limitations: No universal weight limit or ban on all twisting/lifting. Fracture-specific impact advice explicitly precautionary.

protocol.execution: Progressive resistance, impact, balance and posture/hip-hinge techniques; distinct contexts, not one execution.
protocol.dose: Box1: resistance 8–12RM building to three sets; start lower intensity for technique. Vertebral/multiple low-trauma fracture impact up to brisk walking is a precaution, not proven harm threshold.
protocol.frequency: Resistance 2–3 days/week; balance at least twice weekly in specified contexts.
protocol.supervision: Individual physiotherapy advice especially with fractures/new training.
protocol.progression: Individual gradual progression with technique and adverse-effect monitoring.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as a validated numeric stopping algorithm.

sources.design: Randomized trial; 101 women; 49 HiRIT,52 control. Outcome measurer unblinded, BMD verified by blinded investigator; selected population and unequal supervision.
sources.population: Otherwise healthy postmenopausal women >58 years, hip/spine T-score <−1.0; screened for conditions/drugs influencing bone/function. Recent fracture/back pain excluded.
sources.comparator: 8 months twice-weekly 30-minute unsupervised low-load home exercise: walking, lunges, calf raises, raises/shrugs, stretches, progression to 3kg.
sources.coInterventions: Stratification by established osteoporosis medication; participants on/off medication included.
sources.outcomes: At 8 months LS BMD change 2.9±2.8% vs −1.2±2.8% (p<0.001); FN 0.3±2.6% vs −1.9±2.6% (p=0.004). These are changes±SD, not confidence intervals; no fracture-reduction effect established.
sources.uncertainty: Small selected sample, surrogate outcomes; not powered for rare fracture harms; study registration after recruitment had begun.
sources.harms: One minor lower-back spasm in HiRIT, missing 2/70 sessions; summary claim of no adverse events is broader than this reported event.
sources.limitations: Cannot transfer >80–85%1RM lifting or drop landings to unsupervised app users, acute/recent fractures or excluded comorbidity groups.

protocol.execution: Deadlift, overhead press, back squat and jumping chin-up with drop landing; underhand shoulder-width overhead bar, jump/pull then drop and land as heavily as comfortable.
protocol.dose: 30min; resistance 5×5 at >80–85%1RM after familiarisation; up to 2 deadlift warm-up sets at 50–70%1RM.
protocol.progression: First month bodyweight/low-load technique; all reached four movements within2months; later load progression maintained target relative effort.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as a reproducible numeric symptom algorithm.

access.details: Complete article text retrieved and relevant population, methods, results, harms and limitations inspected.

sources.design: Evidence and consensus guideline deriving risk-stratified fracture-prevention training, not one trial.
sources.population: Community-dwelling men/postmenopausal women≥45, varying BMD, fractures and fall risk; institutionalized/younger populations outside scope.
sources.coInterventions: Risk-dependent pharmacological treatment and other fracture management.
sources.outcomes: Supports bone strength/fall prevention exercise; optimal single fracture-prevention protocol remains unknown.
sources.uncertainty: Selected cohorts and outcomes; consensus/evidence grades vary; article excludes detailed acute vertebral-fracture guidance.
sources.harms: Safety section specifies high spinal loading concerns; rare harms/reporting limits prevent universal safety conclusions.
sources.limitations: Risk strata differ: restrictions on dynamic high back-extension/flexion loading coexist with supervised low-stimulus trunk exercise in fracture/fall-risk cohorts. No diagnosis-only ban on all trunk movement.

protocol.execution: Risk-stratified resistance, impact, balance/functional and fall-response training.
protocol.dose: Initial conditioning examples <70%1RM; after adaptation higher bone-loading phases. These are guideline contexts, not a personal load cap.
protocol.frequency: At least2sessions/week for bone strength; about3 for fall prevention.
protocol.supervision: Competent close supervision for complex falling/landing and frail multiple-fracture cohorts.
protocol.progression: Cautious progressive conditioning first3–6months; avoid explosive/high-velocity movements initially.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as an individually validated numeric symptom algorithm.

sources.title: Postmenopausal spinal osteoporosis: flexion versus extension exercises

access.details: Initially abstract-only. Coordinator subsequently rendered and visually inspected all four scanned pages (593–596) from https://therapilates.com/PDF/sinaki.pdf using PDFium and the local image viewer; source has no text layer.

integrity.method: Primary indexed metadata/abstract inspected and current guideline context compared; no DOI verified. No registry-wide correction/retraction search for this old record.
integrity.result: Correction/retraction status not fully verified; no replacement established. This historical study is weak direct harm context, not definitive proof.

sources.design: Retrospective review; exercise choice followed the treating physiatrist’s method, not random allocation. Radiograph comparisons were blinded to prescription.
sources.population: 59 women age49–60 with postmenopausal spinal osteoporosis and back pain.
sources.comparator: Extension n25,flexion n9,combined n19,no therapeutic exercise n6.
sources.coInterventions: Infrared heat and massage in all programs; shared posture/lifting advice, not separately tested.
sources.outcomes: Additional radiographic wedging/compression: extension16%, flexion89%, combined53%, noexercise67%. Flexion versus extension p<0.001; no adjusted risk or confidence interval.
sources.followUp: One to six years. Body reports no-exercise mean2.3years; abstract rounds group means to1.4–2years.
sources.uncertainty: Small unequal groups, clinician selection, historical diagnosis and unequal follow-up limit causal interpretation.
sources.harms: Radiographic wedging/compression was the adverse outcome; broader surveillance not described.
sources.limitations: No universal safe angle/load or causal claim about every bend follows.

protocol.execution: Extension: prone or seated spinal-extensor work. Flexion: sit-ups and seated forward bending. Some no-exercise participants used abdominal isometrics.
protocol.dose: not reported as sets, repetitions or holds
protocol.frequency: not reported for this cohort; discussion frequency refers to another cited study
protocol.supervision: Physiatrist prescribed; session supervision not reported.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported; shared historical lifting/posture advice was not a tested threshold.

gaps: Independent clinical review absent. All mappings/rules/requests are candidates; no therapeutic release, clinical approval or universally safe exercise claim.
Source doses describe studied or recommended contexts, not individual app prescriptions. No generic five-second stretch progression or strength-set credit for stretching.
Coexisting conditions, equipment, independently selected joint limits and user-confirmed starting load remain separate constraints; no restriction may be relaxed to fill an empty workout.
LIFTMOR exact lift mechanics/artwork need verification; thesis-carried text is not asserted to be the final corrected typeset version. Known2019 erratum recorded.
Restriction evidence mostly consensus and risk stratification; no validated universal numeric ROM/weight cap or individual stopping rule.

DVO2026 contains conditional differences across risk strata, including high spinal-load contraindication versus lower-stimulus supervised trunk exercise; do not flatten into contradictory diagnosis-only rules.
